findings.evidence: V3 has the SvelteKit init hook call getConfig() and rely on ConfigError's message (variable names only) to give the 'clear message' of OB7. boot-failfast asserts that the variable's name is printed. A4 (jade-alt, built after jade-8v4) adds uncaughtException and unhandledRejection handlers that 'write an error line and exit 1'. A1 says that 'an error's message and its other properties are never written'. adapter-node awaits server.init() at module top level, so a ConfigError thrown in init rejects module evaluation. Node then passes it to the registered uncaughtException handler (the hooks module, and so the handlers, are loaded before init runs). The output becomes an error line with err_type ConfigError and no variable names. In APP_ENV=development the raw error is printed too, but in the failfast case APP_ENV itself may be the missing variable. From jade-alt on, OB7's check fails, or the implementer has to invent a bypass of the closed logger without a design.
findings.fix: Specify the config-failure path explicitly. init (or a wrapper around getConfig in hooks) catches ConfigError, writes one fixed lifecycle line (for example msg 'config_error' with allowlisted keys 'missing' and 'invalid' whose validator accepts only names from the config schemas' key set), or writes the value-free ConfigError text to stderr, then calls process.exit(1) before any generic handler sees it. State that the uncaughtException handler must not swallow it. Keep boot-failfast in every gate from jade-alt on, and add a log-schema case for the config_error line.

findings.evidence: The check 'ports 3000 and 5432 refuse connections from the host' uses fixed host ports. compose.dev.yml publishes the development database on 127.0.0.1:${JADE_DEV_DB_PORT:-5432}, and the gate from jade-80h on runs `pnpm test` (which needs that database up) before `pnpm test:infra`, as does `pnpm ci:local`. With the default port the assertion fails although compose.prod.yml publishes nothing.
findings.fix: Assert non-exposure on the stack itself: `docker compose -p <test project> port` or inspect shows no published port for app and db. Also check that the containers' service ports are not reachable on the host ports the test allocated, rather than probing fixed 3000 and 5432.

findings.evidence: The ADR 0024 Consequences bullet says 'ADR 0015 is unchanged', but the same section appends a Consequences bullet to docs/adr/0015-tooling.md, and AC13 counts 0015-tooling.md as a changed path. The durable record would contradict itself.
findings.fix: Reword the bullet to 'ADR 0015's Decision is unchanged (one Consequences line points here)', or drop the 0015 edit and keep only the README index row.

findings.evidence: ensureAppRole() runs as step 2 of every migrate() and sets jade_app's password each time. Roles are cluster-wide, while the advisory lock of step 1 is per database. Parallel integration files (migrate.test's runners and db-scripts.test's reset and migrate) can therefore issue concurrent ALTER ROLE on the same pg_authid row, which Postgres can reject with 'tuple concurrently updated'. That makes the harness flaky.
findings.fix: Make ensureAppRole a no-op when the role exists with the expected verifier, or serialize it with a cluster-wide mechanism, for example an advisory lock taken in the shared 'postgres' maintenance database. Add a test that runs two migrations on different databases at once.
findings.path: plan section 9, U2 and U3 (ensureAppRole) with U7 (parallel test files)

findings.evidence: D3 runs compose.prod.yml locally with the .env from `pnpm env:init`. That same file serves `pnpm dev`, with host-side DATABASE_URL and MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL pointing at 127.0.0.1:<dev port> and APP_ENV=development. D2 says app and migrate 'receive' both URLs, but does not say whether Compose passes them through (wrong host inside the container) or builds them from password variables with host `db`. It also does not say which APP_ENV the local prod stack gets: with APP_ENV=development, its /dev/ routes would be live. Separately, backend is internal:true, so the nightly backup to object storage (jade-6o3) has no outbound route, and the consumer table does not mention this.
findings.fix: State that compose.prod.yml builds the container URLs as postgres://jade_app:${JADE_APP_DB_PASSWORD:?}@db:5432/jade (and the owner URL likewise), and never passes the host-side URLs through. State the APP_ENV the local prod stack runs under, and check it in compose-config.test. Add jade-6o3 to section 15 with the note that a backup service must sit on a network with egress.

findings.evidence: tools/ci/clean-clone.sh clones HEAD, so it tests the last commit. In section 16 the gate (step 3) runs before the commit (step 4). If `pnpm ci:clean-clone` is part of the pre-commit evidence, it validates the previous bead's tree, not the bead under review, even though AC4 says 'on that bead's commit'.
findings.fix: State that ci:clean-clone runs after the bead's commit and that its exit status is recorded against that commit SHA. Alternatively, have the script clone a temporary commit or stash of the working tree and record which tree it tested.
